claims.claim: ⚠️ **Let the child choose their own position, and do not upset them.** Decompensation can be rapid and needs emergency airway management.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infants are most at risk**, and a child with a pre-existing narrow airway may fully obstruct with otherwise minor swelling.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Croup is the most common cause, but always consider others.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Let the child settle quietly on a parent's lap**, and observe closely with minimal examination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hypoxia is a late sign. Total obstruction rapidly progresses to unconsciousness and cardiorespiratory arrest.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Presentations often overlap, particularly the bacterial causes.** **Croup:** young child (rare under 3 months), sudden harsh barking cough, hoarse voice, stridor; may be febrile but systemically well.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Epiglottitis:** inadequate Hib immunisation or immunocompromise; high fever, systemically unwell; muffled voice, neck hyperextension, drooling; **cough absent**; stridor (or stertor) that is expiratory and low-pitched.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bacterial tracheitis:** follows a recent URTI; the child is systemically unwell and the illness is more severe and progresses rapidly; trachea markedly tender; thick secretions.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Inhaled foreign body:** young child, very sudden onset, a coughing or choking episode (may be unwitnessed), possibly unilateral chest signs or wheeze.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Anaphylaxis:** facial and tongue swelling, wheeze, urticaria, allergen exposure, haemodynamic compromise.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Retropharyngeal abscess:** fever with sore throat; neck pain with stiffness or torticollis; posterior pharyngeal wall full and red; dysphagia; drooling.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Quinsy:** severe, often unilateral sore throat, hot-potato voice, trismus, medially displaced tonsil and deviated uvula.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ludwig angina:** swollen, tender floor of mouth, submandibular swelling, with a facial laceration or dental abscess. **Airway burns:** facial burns, singed nasal hairs, sooty sputum.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Moderate to severe obstruction: at high risk of complete obstruction if upset, sedated or repositioned. Defer investigations until the airway is secure.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If IV access is needed, use analgesia and distraction.** **Croup needs no investigations.** Imaging to help locate the obstruction: CT, or an X-ray of the chest and/or soft-tissue neck.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat emergency airway management here as a difficult airway, led by the most senior clinician available**, with anaesthetic or ENT support.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oxygen may improve saturations but does not relieve the obstruction.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider nebulised adrenaline for temporary relief in any life-threatening obstruction**, while awaiting definitive measures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider giving 0.6 mg/kg dexamethasone (max 16 mg)** by the IM, IV or oral route to reduce swelling if present.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intubate with a tube ½–1 size below the usual age-appropriate size.** Cuffed tubes allow inflation if a leak develops as the obstruction resolves; gaseous induction is preferred.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat the specific cause**; for bacterial infections follow local antimicrobial guidelines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderate obstruction: involve the paediatric team. Severe obstruction or a known difficult airway: anaesthetics and/or ENT.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer** if the child may deteriorate and need airway management beyond local capability.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** the cause is identified, signs have resolved or are mild and improving, and follow-up is in place.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute upper airway obstruction' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_upper_airway_obstruction/, retrieved 2026-09-23
